title: Demon Dragon
paragraphs: “I’ve been thinking, but our group’s weapons are a bit unbalanced, aren’t they?”
“There are a lot of claws.”
“Well, when the Filolials each use their own preferred weapons…”
“Gaelion can use a staff too!” Rival spoke up here, trying to show off his versatility.
How shameless!
I’ll crush him!
“Sakura uses swords! Ren doesn’t even come close!”
“Hey!”
“Motoyasu, calm down! You’re causing unnecessary conflict by trying to compete!”
“Hmm? I can beat Gaelion.”
Sakura swung her dual swords around with a flourish.
“Are you saying that’s better than me?! It’s just play-fighting!”
“It’s not even a contest!”
To me, Sakura is far superior to Ren.
“What!?”
“Ren, calm down!”
“It’s Motoyasu!”
“Guh…”
“You know full well that Ren is actually better because of all the training, right?”
Father held Ren down. Hmph… You’re someone who even loses to Éclair. I won’t let you belittle Sakura.
“What kind of weapon does Naofumi want Gaelion to use? If Naofumi asks, Gaelion will definitely learn it!”
“I want to learn too!”
Rival and Big Sister’s friend tilted their heads as they spoke. It’s fine for Big Sister’s friend, but you, Rival, just stay quiet!
“You’re both fine as you are now.”
As we chatted while taking down hordes of demons, we reached a crossroads where Rival and the Filolials all turned to the left simultaneously.
“What’s wrong?”
Father and Itsuki, who had been calming Ren down, noticed the Filolials’ unusual behavior.
“I feel something… kind of a disturbance over there.”
“There’s a flow of magic over there… and I can sense a disruption in the dragon veins too. It’s the same kind of power I felt when we broke the barrier.”
“Then maybe there’s someone over there generating a barrier? In game terms, it would be best to explore the treasure vaults first, but…”
“But the only sign of treasure is coming from that direction.”
Rival’s words made Father fall into thought.
“Maybe they put the leftovers in the treasure vault we already visited?”
“I wonder… Either way, it seems better to go left at this crossroads.”
“What do you think? Maybe Rival’s intuition is just off this time.”
“Either way, if there’s a boss ahead, it might be best to defeat it first.”
Father folded his arms, seeming deep in thought.
“What’s got you so worried?”

“In game terms, there are those types of dungeons where once you clear them, you can never go back, right? If the boss ahead is what’s keeping this place intact, the whole thing might collapse after we take it down.”
Itsuki nodded, seeming to understand. I’d like to understand too.
“But maybe I’m overthinking it, like it’s a game…”
“Either way, if we trust Gaelion’s words, we have no choice but to go.”
“Yeah, I guess so. We should explore as many of the treasure vaults as possible on the way.”
“That’s true. This… really gets a gamer’s blood pumping.”
“If there’s someone pulling the strings here, I’d like to know who they are.”

With that, we headed in the direction indicated by Rival and the Filolials. Even after that, the frequency of demon appearances remained high. But to us now, they were nothing more than small fry. Thanks to the new skills, even Father and the others could handle them easily. Following the path, we relied on the instincts of Rival and the Filolials to guide us. Ah, Father was mapping everything by hand. At times like this, Father always took care of the meticulous work. The map was turning out quite well. The doctor seemed to be helping by adding details as well.
“We’re pretty close now. I think there’s a force field up ahead.”
“Does that mean it’s a boss battle?”
“I’m not sure… but… yeah. I think I can sense the presence of the Dragon Emperor.”
“A dragon?”
“Hmm…”
Rival tilted his head in response to Father’s question. Be more clear!
“I’m not sure. It feels more like fragments of it.”
“What about the treasure vault?”
“So far, aside from the first treasure vault, all we’ve found are places that seem more like storage rooms. We don’t know where they’ve hidden it, but it’s definitely ahead.”
“Yeah.”
“Whatever’s there, I’ll smash through it.”
“Ah… yeah. If we’re thinking in game terms, maybe the treasure appears after the boss is defeated?”
“Well, we’ve already gotten plenty of powerful weapons, so even if it’s something that becomes unobtainable after clearing the place, it’s fine.”
Hearing Itsuki’s response, Father snapped out of his thoughts and gave a slightly wry smile.
“Even though this is another world, it’s not a game… I keep forgetting that sometimes.”
“Now that you mention it… that’s true. Worst-case scenario, we can work with the Queen or Faubrey to dig it out later. For now, let’s focus on finding a way out.”
“Yeah, I’m getting tired of this.”
“Whatever comes our way, I’ll take it down quickly.”
And so, we made our way toward the source of what Rival and the Filolials had sensed. As we moved forward, something resembling an ominous cloud began to drift toward us from the end of the corridor.

We proceeded forward and entered a large… open hall that looked like an altar. It seemed that the path continued beyond the altar. The walls looked different from what we had seen before. They had a sinister color, pulsing and glowing in a distorted way, emphasizing the eerie atmosphere.

Yes, that’s right. The walls looked even more corrupted than the sinister, polluted walls of Melromarc we had encountered before. After taking down the attacking demons, we entered the open hall. At the far end, there was a large throne. Sitting on it was a creature that looked somewhat like a dragon.
“A dragon?”
“Hmm…? I’m not really sure…”
Just like Rival, dragons seem to like thrones.
“Either way, we have no choice but to go forward.”
“Got it. Everyone, get ready to fight at any moment.”
“Of course.”
“A dragon boss at the end of a dungeon… how cliché.”
“Come on, let’s go.”
Ignoring Itsuki’s comment, we approached the dragon.
“I didn’t expect a dragon to be here.”
Rival looked at the creature sitting on the throne… It had a ridiculously bulky physique for a dragon. A macho dragon. It was more of a draconic humanoid.
“Gruuuuuuu…”
“It sounds like a dragon zombie.”
“Something about it feels different.”
Really? I couldn’t tell.
“GraaaaAAAAAAA!”
The dragon stood up and opened its mouth, preparing to unleash a pitch-black breath. It seemed to have zero intention of negotiating.
“Looks like that thing’s ready for a fight!”
“Then we’ll just have to fight back.”
“So, it has no intention of talking things out?”
“Apparently not. Kuro! Let’s go!”
“Yeah! But that thing… I’ve analyzed it as a Devil’s Imitation Dragon—an imitation of a dragon emperor corrupted by demons.”
“That’s… a mouthful!”
I glared at the dragon in front of me. And then, its name appeared before me. The Corrupted Fallen Dragon—Devil Drac—Crow.
“I can’t see its name properly. It’s bugging out.”
“I know this isn’t a game… but still…”
“Um, Kawasumi, that enemy… it doesn’t really feel like a dragon.”
“Is that so?”
Yuki nodded in response to that question. It was rare for the Filolials to explain information about dragons.
“Yes, if it were a dragon, I would feel the same unease and irritation as I do when I’m near the Dragon Emperor, but the enemy in front of us feels a little different.”
